Question: Have you ever had to take action against someone who merely photographed or recorded you without consent? What did you do?
Answer: If I am out in public, as others have said, I should be aware that others could photograph me, and they would be perfectly within their rights to do so. I would not care at all. On the other hand, if someone chose to be intrusive and follow me around taking pictures OF ME, I would consider that to be stalking, but merely taking a picture where I happen to be in the shot is not enough for me to even notice or care about it. Not everything is worth complaining to authorities.

Question: Can information from any version of Wikipedia be used as a reference source for college research papers in English?
Answer: Only the Quora Prompt Generator would ask this question. Any sentient being (e.g., a human) who knows anything about academic research would know Wikipedia is not a peer-reviewed source, and professors and academic advisers explicitly warn students not to use Wikipedia or other similar sources as references. I say this as someone who has edited over 1,000 Wikipedia articles, written tons of academic papers especially for my master’s, and edited doctoral dissertations under the guidance of the students’ advisers. On the other hand, as Bill Smith noted in a comment, many excellent Wikipedia articles include a “References” section at the bottom of the article, and you can read those primary sources, which you could cite as references in your college research paper, even though you cannot actually cite the Wikipedia article itself. —Sarah Madden, #8413, Written and ©Copyrighted ❤️ 19 June 2024 QUESTION: Can information from any version of Wikipedia be used as a reference source for college research papers in English?
